content:
Toxicology reports obtained by multiple media outlets on Tuesday showed that actress Hayden Panettiere died from the toxic effects of fentanyl and several other substances.

An autopsy was performed by the Greenville County coroner's office in South Carolina, and the cause of death was ruled accidental. She passed away at an apartment in Greenville at the age of 36.

The report noted that 4-ANPP, alprazolam, methocarbamol, and quetiapine were also detected in her system and contributed to her death.

The coroner's report stated: "There were no signs of trauma that could have caused death found during the autopsy."

According to information from the US Drug Enforcement Administration, 4-ANPP is a controlled substance commonly found in the illicit manufacturing of fentanyl. Alprazolam is more commonly known by the brand name Xanax and is used to treat anxiety and panic disorders. Methocarbamol is a prescription muscle relaxant, while quetiapine is prescribed to treat schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and major depressive disorder.

ABC News reported at the time, citing sources familiar with the matter, that several days after her passing, the US Drug Enforcement Administration joined forces with local and state officials to investigate.

The star of "Heroes" and "Nashville" was found unconscious in the company of her on-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson and his brother Zach Hickerson. According to a heavily redacted police report, paramedics performed "prolonged" resuscitation efforts upon arriving at the scene, but she was ultimately pronounced dead at the location.

Panettiere's relationship with Brian Hickerson had long been characterized as volatile and unhealthy, with the latter having been arrested multiple times since 2019 on suspicion of domestic violence against her.

According to TMZ, the two brothers were not invited to the memorial held for Panettiere in Malibu, California over the weekend.
